title: Add Structured Request Logging Middleware with Request ID Propagation
description: Provides automatic JSON‑structured logging for every incoming request, including method, URL, status, response time and a unique request ID that is attached to the request and response objects. This improves observability, simplifies tracing across services, and meets compliance requirements without adding external dependencies.
testCases: Verify that each request generates a unique request ID and that the ID is accessible via req.id and res.setHeader('X-Request-Id')
Confirm that the logger outputs a single JSON line containing method, url, status, responseTime, and requestId for successful and error responses
Ensure that disabling the logger via configuration results in no log output but does not affect request handling
acceptance: When the middleware is enabled, every HTTP request results in a single well‑formed JSON log line containing the required fields; the same request ID appears in the log, the response header, and is reachable via req.id. Disabling the middleware produces no logs and does not alter response behavior. All tests pass and existing routing/middleware functionality remains unaffected.
reason: Production systems need reliable, structured logs for monitoring, debugging, and traceability. Adding built‑in request logging eliminates the need for third‑party logging libraries, aligns with the framework's zero‑dependency philosophy, and provides immediate value to developers using yantraverse.
